title: Creamy Pancetta & Mushroom Tagliatelle
summary: Rendered pancetta fat is the savoury base for this creamy mushroom sauce. The key is searing the mushrooms properly to develop a deep, nutty flavour.

steps.text: Put a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the pancetta; you do not need oil. Cook for {timer:5-7}, until the fat renders and the cubes are crisp. Lift out the pancetta and leave the fat in the pan.

Add the butter to the rendered fat and turn the heat up to medium-high. Add the mushrooms and cook undisturbed for {timer:2-3} to brown, then stir. Add the onion and cook for {timer:2-3}, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted water for 1 minute less than the packet instructions. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
If using wine, pour it into the mushroom pan and let it bubble. Lower the heat to medium, pour in the cream and simmer gently for {timer:2}.
Stir in the Parmesan and black pepper. Taste and add salt if needed; the pancetta is salty.
Return the pasta and crispy pancetta to the sauce and toss vigorously for {timer:1}, adding pasta water if it is too thick. Turn off the heat, stir in the parsley and serve straight away.

tips: Guanciale is an excellent substitute for the pancetta. Do not overcrowd the mushrooms: if your pan is small, cook them in batches. Starchy pasta water is the secret to restaurant-quality pasta. Cream at room temperature blends in more smoothly without splitting.
